title: Change management: current, interim and target states
blurb: Define change management, trace the move from current through interim to target state, and explain why adoption drives benefits.
question: A freight company's project delivered every scanner and app on time, yet six months later drivers still use paper and no savings have appeared. What has the project neglected?

teach.h: What change management means in PRINCE2 7
teach.body: Formally, change management is the means by which an organization transitions from its current state to its target state, and effective leadership is needed to deliver it. In plain English: a project does not just build things; it moves people and the organization from 'how we work now' to 'how we will work', sometimes through stepping stones on the way.

steps.label: Interim state
steps.sub: a stepping stone, such as a pilot

teach.caption: Interim states are optional: the change management approach plans the move 'through any interim states'.

teach.h: Why it matters: benefits need adoption
teach.body: Projects deliver outputs. Outcomes are the result of change, normally affecting real-world behaviour, and benefits are the measurable improvements that come from outcomes. If people do not adopt the new ways of working, the outputs sit unused, the outcomes never happen and the benefits are not realized. Change management is how the project gets people to the target state, not just the products to handover.

teach.h: Where adoption sits in the benefits chain
teach.caption: Projects deliver outputs; outcomes and most benefits come after people change how they work.

head: Characteristic
Example of a change
rows: Drivers scan instead of signing paper
A new data team in the depot
Staff skilled in the scanner app
teach.caption: The change management approach describes the characteristics of each state, highlighting those that change (manual 3.2.1).

teach.body: Ashcombe Freight wants drivers to record deliveries on handheld scanners. Project manager Daniel Price describes the current state (paper notes, disputes settled by phone) and the target state (every delivery scanned, disputes settled from data). Senior user Meera Shah agrees an interim state: one pilot depot on scanners while the others stay on paper. Training and a help line support each step, and the project tracks whether drivers actually stop using paper.

teach.text: In PRINCE2 7, 'change management' means organizational transition (part of the people element). It is NOT change control. Controlling changes to the project baseline belongs to the issues practice and the issue management approach.

items: Change management: how an organization transitions from the current state to the target state (manual 3.2.1).
The move may pass through interim states, such as a pilot or a phased roll-out.
Effective leadership is needed to deliver the change.
Outputs only turn into outcomes and benefits when people adopt new ways of working.
Each state can be described by its routines, practices, processes, culture, responsibilities, structure and capabilities.

summary: You can now define change management as the transition from current to target state, possibly through interim states, and explain why benefits depend on people adopting new ways of working. You can also keep it apart from change control, which belongs to the issues practice.

A.q: Which statement defines change management in PRINCE2 7?
options: The procedure for assessing and approving changes to the baseline
The means by which an organization moves from its current to its target state
The control of product versions through configuration and version records
The delegation of authority to approve requests for change to a change authority
A.why: Change management is the means by which an organization transitions from the current state to the target state (manual 3.2.1).

whyNot.0: Assessing and approving changes to the baseline is change control, part of the issues practice.
whyNot.2: Version and configuration control of products is part of managing baselines in the issues practice.
whyNot.3: Delegating approval of requests for change is part of the issues practice (change authority), not change management.

A.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. Change management is the means by which an organization transitions from the current state to the [?] state.
options: interim
baseline
operational
target
A.why: PRINCE2 describes change management as the transition from the current state to the target state, possibly through interim states.

whyNot.0: Interim states are stepping stones on the way; the destination is the target state.
whyNot.1: A baseline is the approved set of products under change control, not an organizational state.
whyNot.2: 'Operational state' is not the PRINCE2 term for the destination of the transition.

options: The organization's position before the project begins
The approved version of products subject to change control
The planned period between two management stages
A stepping stone between the current and target states
A.why: An organization may move from the current state through one or more interim states (for example a pilot) before reaching the target state.

whyNot.0: The position before the project is the current state.
whyNot.1: Approved product versions under change control form the project baseline.
whyNot.2: Management stages are a planning and control idea; interim states describe the organization during transition.

B.q: Why is change management important to a project's success?
options: It ensures that changes to the baseline are approved by the project board
It replaces the business case once the products have been delivered
Benefits come from outcomes, which need people to adopt new ways of working
It allows the board to skip stage boundaries during the transition
B.why: Outputs only lead to outcomes and benefits when people change how they work, so the transition to the target state must be led and managed.

whyNot.0: Approving baseline changes is change control in the issues practice, and approval can be delegated to a change authority.
whyNot.1: The business case stays in use and is updated through the project; change management does not replace it.
whyNot.3: Stage boundaries remain decision points; change management does not remove them.

B.q:
Which two statements about change management are correct?
1. Effective leadership is needed to deliver the change.
2. Change management is handled by the issues practice.
3. An organization may pass through interim states before the target state.
4. The target state is reached as soon as the outputs are handed over.
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
B.why: PRINCE2 says effective leadership is needed (1) and the transition may go through interim states (3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: the issues practice handles change control; change management is part of the people element.
whyNot.2: Both are false: change management is people element, and handing over outputs is not the same as people working in the new way.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: the target state needs people to adopt the change, not just receive products.

B.q: A logistics firm's project aims to cut delivery disputes. Which of these is an OUTCOME rather than an output or a benefit?
options: Drivers recording every delivery on a scanner
The handheld scanners delivered by the supplier
A 15% fall in the cost of handling disputes
The training guide written for the scanner app
B.why: An outcome is the result of change, normally affecting real-world behaviour: drivers working in the new way is an outcome.

whyNot.1: The scanners are products the project delivers, so they are outputs.
whyNot.2: A measurable improvement resulting from an outcome is a benefit.
whyNot.3: A training guide is a product of the project, so it is an output.

C.q: During transition, a logistics firm runs one depot on scanners while the other depots stay on paper. Which statement is correct?
options: The pilot is the target state, because new products are in use
The pilot is a baseline change, so it needs a request for change
The pilot is the current state, because most depots are unchanged
The pilot is an interim state on the way to the target state
C.why: A partial roll-out such as a pilot depot is an interim state between the current state and the target state.

whyNot.0: The target state is reached when the organization works in the new way across the intended scope, not at one pilot depot.
whyNot.1: Requests for change concern changes to approved baseline products; a planned pilot is part of the transition, not a baseline change.
whyNot.2: The current state is how the organization worked before the transition began.

C.q: When planning the transition, which factor does PRINCE2 suggest considering?
options: The skills and capabilities needed during and after the transition
The number of quality review meetings planned for each product
The version-numbering scheme used for baselined products
The amount of contingency held in the project's risk budget
C.why: Considerations include the skills and capabilities needed during and after transition, the areas of the organizational ecosystem impacted, key relationships, the evolving culture and how best to transition (manual 3.2.1).

whyNot.1: Quality review planning belongs to the quality practice.
whyNot.2: Version numbering of baselined products is part of the issues practice and configuration control.
whyNot.3: The risk budget funds risk responses under the risk practice.

C.q: A project delivered all its outputs on time and to budget, but months later staff still use the old process and no benefits have appeared. What has been missing?
options: Tighter change control over the project baseline
Effective change management towards the target state
A larger change budget for requests for change
More frequent checkpoint reports from team managers
C.why: Delivering outputs is not enough: the organization has not transitioned to the target state, so outcomes and benefits have not followed.

whyNot.0: Change control protects the baseline; the problem here is people not adopting the change.
whyNot.2: A change budget funds approved changes to the baseline; it does not move people to new ways of working.
whyNot.3: Checkpoint reports track work package progress; the outputs were delivered, so progress reporting was not the gap.

reteach.title: Moving house, not just buying furniture
reteach.question: If a family buys new furniture but keeps living in the old house, have they moved?

blocks.body: Buying furniture is like delivering outputs. Moving in, changing routines and living in the new house is like reaching the target state. A family might stay with relatives for a few weeks first: that is an interim state. Change management is the planned, led journey from the old house to the new life, not just the shopping.

blocks.text: Changing the furniture order after it is agreed would be change control (the issues practice). Getting the family to live differently is change management (the people element).

explain.body: The current state is how the organization works today. The target state is the organizational state the project needs for it to meet its objectives. Change management is the transition between them.

test.q: What does the target state describe?
options: The organization as it works today, before the project starts
The approved products held under change control
The organizational state the project needs to meet its objectives
The stage at which the project board authorizes project closure
test.why: The target state is the organizational state required for the project to meet its objectives.

whyNot.0: How the organization works before the project is the current state.
whyNot.1: Approved products under change control are the project baseline.
whyNot.3: Closure is a point in the project lifecycle, not the organizational state the change aims for.

explain.body: Large changes are often made in steps: a pilot, a phased roll-out, or old and new running side by side. Each step is an interim state between the current and target states.

test.q: A bank moves half its branches to a new process while the rest keep the old one. How is this best described?
options: An interim state in the transition
The target state of the change
A concession on an off-specification
An exception to stage tolerance
test.why: Running part of the organization on the new process is a stepping stone, so it is an interim state.

whyNot.1: The target state is reached when the intended new way of working is in place.
whyNot.2: A concession is an off-specification accepted without corrective action (issues practice).
whyNot.3: An exception is a forecast breach of tolerance; a planned partial roll-out is not one.

explain.body: Outputs are products. Outcomes are the result of change in behaviour and circumstances. Benefits are measurable improvements from outcomes. Without adoption, the chain stops at outputs.

test.q: Which is a benefit rather than an output or outcome?
options: A new online booking system
Patients booking their own appointments
A 20% cut in missed appointments
The user guide for reception staff
test.why: A benefit is a measurable improvement resulting from an outcome.

whyNot.0: The booking system is a product, so it is an output.
whyNot.1: Patients behaving differently is an outcome.
whyNot.3: A user guide is a product of the project, so it is an output.

explain.body: PRINCE2 states that effective leadership is required to deliver change. Leaders motivate, persuade and co-create so that people choose to work in the new way, rather than having it imposed.

test.q: According to PRINCE2, what is required to deliver change from the current state to the target state?
options: A delegated change authority
An approved exception plan
Effective leadership
A detailed set of team plans
test.why: PRINCE2 says effective leadership is required to deliver change (manual 3.2.1).

whyNot.0: A change authority approves requests for change within limits (issues practice).
whyNot.1: An exception plan responds to a forecast tolerance breach.
whyNot.3: Team plans organize the work inside work packages; PRINCE2 names leadership, not planning detail, as what delivers change.
